correctness.rationale: From the stated payoff u_i=-r_i-c s_i, raising one's bid overtakes exactly earlier-index zero bidders and later-index one bidders, giving Δ_i=A_i-c. The adjacent identity A_(i+1)-A_i=1-s_i-s_(i+1) is exact. Adjacent bid switches force A=c, hence integer prices, and any repeat after the switch would violate a Nash inequality; the remaining suffix alternates. Solving its transition index produces two feasible prefix words at each r=1,...,n-1; constant profiles show all zeros is the sole equilibrium for c>n-1 and all ones is never an equilibrium when c>0. Both the n=2 and c=n-1 boundaries are included without duplicate counting. Independently reconstructed direct utilities and exhaustive best responses across 112 (n,c) configurations, n=2..9, corroborated all equilibria; finite enumeration does not prove the universal classification.

value.rationale: The exact complete-conflict family is the first natural robustness test for the priced-priority equilibrium model: it shows all low generic noninteger prices have no pure Nash equilibrium, while each integer price up to n−1 has exactly two and sufficiently high price has one. This all-size sharp classification is a motivated structural equilibrium fact, not a sampled numerical anomaly.

limitations: Finite checks are corroborative; no extension to heterogeneous fees, higher priority levels, partial conflict graphs or mixed equilibria.
